subject.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication

question: Should Crabline adopt this fail-closed ownership, identity, and Windows ACL contract for existing OpenClaw private-state paths?
rationale: The patch intentionally turns previously tolerated ownership or ACL drift into runtime rejection and changes security-sensitive cross-platform filesystem semantics, so automation cannot choose the permanent compatibility and recovery contract.

options.title: Approve after cross-platform proof
options.body: Adopt the fail-closed contract after native Windows focused output and explicit legacy-path recovery expectations are reviewed.

options.title: Narrow the initial landing
options.body: Land only the fully proven platform behavior and defer the remaining ACL boundary until equivalent host proof exists.

options.title: Defer the boundary change
options.body: Keep current behavior until maintainers define a migration-compatible ownership and ACL policy.

recommendation.title: Approve after cross-platform proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the fail-closed contract after native Windows focused output and explicit legacy-path recovery expectations are reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository member authored the complete focused hardening series and is the strongest evidenced routing candidate.
